sanjay (eng-runtime): quick heads-up — noticed a small numeric drift + perf regression after switching kernel selector to flash-attn-v2 for long seqs when KV cache is enabled. delta shows up only with bf16 on A100 and only for sequences > 2048.

maria (eng-runtime): can you paste the numbers? perf regression magnitude? :thinking:

sanjay (eng-runtime): perf: 1.8% slower end-to-end on throughput for 8k tokens, latency p95 up ~12ms. Numeric: L2 diff between baseline and flash-v2 ~1.2e-3 on logits after softmax, some outputs diverge in top-5 choices.

kevin (eng-ml): hmm is this numerical instability around softmax's pre-scaling? bf16 + fused kernels can lose exponent headroom. did you see any inf/nan?

sanjay (eng-runtime): no inf/nan, but exp() seems to saturate on some heads. profiling shows larger time spent in fused_softmax_kernel and different warp-level reductions.

anya (eng-runtime): repro command? I'll try locally.

sanjay (eng-runtime): repro attached — run on A100 (single GPU):
```
python -m examples/serve_repro --model redwood/test-bert --seq_len 8192 --batch 1 --cache --kernel-selector flash-v2 --dtype bf16
```
Compare outputs with kernel-selector=flash-v1 and dtype=fp16.

kevin (eng-ml): thanks. i'll run fp16 vs bf16 diff. Could be accumulation precision (sum of exponentials) — try subtracting max before exp (numeric stable softmax) ?

maria (eng-runtime): our fused flash-v2 assumes pre-normalized inputs (we forgot max-subtract in one codepath for paged KV hotpath). possible bug.

jess (eng-sre): if this regresses customer workloads we need a canary rollback plan. recommend a conservative rollout: 10% of traffic on dedicated pools then monitor.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for kernel-selector=flash-v2 on pool 'prod-dedicated-1' (10% traffic).

sanjay (eng-runtime): quick micro-bench results after instrumenting softmax in kernel: adding max-subtract -> numeric diff drops to 2e-7, perf penalty negligible (~0.3% in kernel time). patch idea below.

maria (eng-runtime): can you paste patch snippet?

sanjay (eng-runtime): patch:
```
// in fused_softmax.cu
float maxv = warp_reduce_max(x);
x -= maxv; // stabilize
x = expf(x * inv_scale);
sum = warp_reduce_sum(x);
output = x / sum;
```

kevin (eng-ml): also saw batch-merging heuristics cause KV misalignment when dynamic padding is used — we were compacting batches differently across kernel variants which made positions shift slightly, leading to mismatched KV indices. that can explain top-k drifts.

anya (eng-runtime): suggested fix: normalize KV indexing to absolute positions before batched merge. simpler: attach global-pos metadata and use it to build merged KV offsets.

maria (eng-runtime): i'm going to add a guarded softmax path for bf16 in flash-v2 and add the global-pos metadata to batching layer. will run internal perf/regression suite.

jess (eng-sre): ping me when canary metrics are in. set alert if token-error-rate or top-1 drift > 0.1% or latency p95 regresses >5%.

sanjay (eng-runtime): thanks. logs/benchmarks uploaded to the perf board: https://internal.redwood/perf/2065432100-kernel-drift

kevin (eng-ml): i'll run evals on prompt suites to confirm quality no-regress after patch. if clean, we can proceed with progressive rollout.

maria (eng-runtime): filing a follow-up PR and test plan. cc @kevin @jess

jess (eng-sre): :thumbsup: keep it tight.
